{{Short description|American mathematician}}
{{Use dmy dates|cs1-dates=ly|date=March 2021}}

[[File:Jessica S. Purcell Oberwolfach 2023.jpg|thumb|Purcell at [[Mathematisches Forschungsinstitut Oberwolfach|Oberwolfach]] in 2023]]
'''Jessica A. Shepherd Purcell''' is an American mathematician specializing in [[low-dimensional topology]] whose research topics have included [[hyperbolic Dehn surgery]] and the [[Jones polynomial]]. She is a professor of mathematics at [[Monash University]] in [[Melbourne]], Australia.{{r|cv}}

==Education==
Purcell credits a high school mathematics teacher, Mr. Pehrson, for her interest in mathematics.{{r|pehrson}} She majored in mathematics as an undergraduate at the [[University of Utah]], with a minor in computer science. She was a co-winner of the 1998 [[Alice T. Schafer Prize|Alice T. Schafer Prize for Excellence in Mathematics by an Undergraduate Woman]] of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]],{{r|schafer98|25schafer}} and graduated [[summa cum laude]] in 1998.{{r|cv}}

After earning a master's degree in mathematics at the [[University of Michigan]] in 1999,{{r|cv}} Purcell completed her Ph.D. at [[Stanford University]] in 2004. Her dissertation, ''Cusp Shapes of Hyperbolic Link Complements and Dehn Filling'', was supervised by [[Steven Kerckhoff]].{{r|cv|mg}}

==Career==
After postdoctoral research at the [[University of Texas at Austin]] and [[University of Oxford]], Purcell became an assistant professor at [[Brigham Young University]] in 2007.{{r|cv}} She was named a Sloan Research Fellow in 2011,{{r|cv|sloan}} and earned tenure at Brigham Young in 2013. After visits to Monash University and at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] as a Von Neumann Fellow, she moved to Monash as an associate professor in 2015, became an ARC Future Fellow in 2017, and was named full professor in 2019.{{r|cv}}

She chaired the Women in Mathematics Special Interest Group of the [[Australian Mathematical Society]] for 2018–2019 and 2019–2020.{{r|austms}}

==Recognition==
Purcell's work has earned international recognition for advancing understanding of geometric structures in three-dimensional spaces, including applications to theoretical physics and pure mathematics. She has received prestigious awards, such as the Alfred P. Sloan Research Fellowship in 2011<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jessica Purcell |url=https://news.byu.edu/news/math-professor-jessica-purcell-wins-prestigious-science-fellowship#:~:text=For%20only%20the%20second%20time%2C%20a%20scientist,Fellowship%20%E2%80%94%20a%20secret%20she%20and%20her |access-date=2025-02-11 |website= BYU news |language=en}}</ref>, the National Science Foundation CAREER Award from 2013 to 2016, and the Von Neumann Fellowship at the Institute for Advanced Study in 2015<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jessica Purcell |url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/jessica-s-purcell|access-date=2025-02-11 |website= Institute for Advanced Study |language=en}}</ref>. 
Purcell was elected a [[List of fellows of the Australian Academy of Science|Fellow of the Australian Academy of Science]] in May 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jessica Purcell |url=https://www.science.org.au/profile/jessica-purcell-0 |access-date=2025-05-26 |website=Australian Academy of Science |language=en}}</ref> She was elected to the 2026 class of Fellows of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/cgi-bin/fellows/fellows_by_year.cgi|title=2026 Class of Fellows of the AMS|publisher=American Mathematical Society|access-date=2025-11-08}}</ref>

==Books==
Purcell is the author of the book ''Hyperbolic Knot Theory'' ([[Graduate Studies in Mathematics]] 209, [[American Mathematical Society]], 2020).{{r|hkt}} With David Futer and [[Efstratia Kalfagianni]] she is a coauthor of ''Guts of Surfaces and the Colored Jones Polynomial'' ([[Lecture Notes in Mathematics]] 2069, Springer, 2012).{{r|guts}}
